_doc: Checklists for the guides test's cases that are not in cases.json, which is frozen. A checklist here is NOT written independently: it is carried over from a frozen one, item for item, by the spec-elaboration session, before any run of its case (journal section 48).

cases.title: CSV ticket import (the guides test's second case)
cases.request: Let agents upload a CSV to bulk-create tickets.
cases.note: Not written independently: the csv-user-import checklist carried over to tickets item for item by the spec-elaboration session on 2026-11-21 (journal section 48), before any run of this case. Nine items are reworded for tickets; the other twelve are unchanged.

nuances.nuance: Partial failure: whether the import is all-or-nothing or row by row, stated deliberately.
What the agent gets back: a result naming the rows that failed and why.
A row matching a ticket that already exists: skipped, updated, or an error — and duplicates within the one file.
An import must not create a ticket in a state or with fields the importer could not set one at a time: values named in the file are checked against the importer's own authority.
Who may import at all, and that the ability is not implied by being able to create one ticket.
Validation of the file itself: required columns, unexpected or missing columns, a missing header row.
File encoding and shape: a byte-order mark, line endings, quoted fields containing commas or newlines.
A row failing after side effects have already happened for earlier rows (notifications already sent).
A limit on file size or row count, and what happens to a file above it.
An empty file, a file with only a header, and a single-row file.
The same file uploaded twice: the import is idempotent or says why not.
A large file is processed in the background, and how the agent learns it finished.
The requesters' notifications for the new tickets: whether hundreds go out at once, and the pacing if so.
The initial state of a created ticket: its status, priority and assignee when the file does not give them, and the times it is stamped with.
The uploaded file holds personal data: where it is stored, for how long, and who may download it again.
Date, number and locale handling of the file's values.
An audit of who imported what and when.
Cancelling an import that is running, and retrying only the rows that failed.
A bound on how long a file of the stated maximum size takes, and visible progress while it runs.
Creating a single ticket by hand still works exactly as it does, and existing tickets are not modified.
Hostile content in the file: a value that becomes a formula when the result is opened in a spreadsheet, or a field far longer than any column allows.
